prompt: Some people believe that childhood is the best stage of happiness.While others believe that a person can enjoy more happiness in other stages of life? Discuss both views and give your opinion?
essay:
Some people argue that youth is the most remarkable and happiest part of individuals’ lives. Others believe that adults are happier inasmuch as they have more freedom and independence. Regardless of these two points, I am convinced that the early years are always an amazing and carefree period; looking back, those years were incredibly special to me. This essay will examine these opinions in detail.

On the one hand, adults have no limits on their actions, which is often referred to as independence and the absence of strong parental guidance; moreover, they shoulder responsibility for their own lives. Adults can do everything that children only dream of doing, ranging from buying a tasty chocolate bar to travelling abroad with friends. To illustrate, I am an operational manager in an international company, and my salary is high enough for travelling abroad. Therefore, I am proud of the chance to be independent of my parents’ financial resources, and this makes me happier. Ultimately, many people perceive freedom and a lack of control as a key factor in happiness.

On the other hand, the formative years are the most significant time span. Children are often surrounded by boundless love and care, with physical and, above all, financial security. Furthermore, children are more impressionable: they tend to be happy simply because of a warm family environment, and even ordinary positive things can capture their attention. To illustrate, one of the most remarkable memories from my early years is that my dad used to pick me up from kindergarten once a week and, instead of going straight home, we went to a café to eat burgers. It was always just the two of us. Such an example clearly illustrates the view that the warmest and most enchanting memories come from the period of growing up, when children seem to be the happiest beings in the world.

In conclusion, while adulthood offers freedom, independence and financial security, I firmly believe that the early stage of life is the happiest. It is a time of unconditional love, carefree days and simple joys, and these are the memories that stay with us long after we grow up.
